messages:
Lena (AE): FYI @Omar @Rina Bright (cust) wants to validate a live cutover from CompetitorX to Redwood for their chat product. Main asks: streaming chunk parity, rate-limit behavior, billing transparency, and GDPR residency. Can we POC with their staging traffic?
Omar (SE): Short answer: yes, but we need to clarify a few things. We can run an in-region hosted POC with IP allowlist + request/response logging turned on for debug. If they require customer KMS or no-key retention, that moves to Dedicated/Private.
Bright (Customer): We need streaming behavior identical to avoid client-side reconnection logic changes. CompetitorX streams in 256-byte chunks, with retry-on-408 semantics.
Rina (Sales Eng): We'll proxy a subset of staging traffic through a compatibility shim that mirrors their headers. That helps catch signal differences. But note: shim preserves HTTP-level streaming, not internal tokenization differences.
Omar (SE): Action: we should capture two artifacts during POC: (1) raw chunk boundaries + timings, (2) full decoded outputs. That lets us measure chunk alignment and latency.
Felix (Eng): For rate-limits: CompetitorX has a per-minute token cap with burst up to 2x. Redwood uses concurrent request tokens + per-minute quota. We'll map their behavior; suggestion: set a soft throttle to emulate CompetitorX.
Jules (Security): Compliance: they asked for EU-only storage and deletion on request. Hosted EU region satisfies general storage, but for deletion controls + attestations (e.g., custom retention windows) we might need Dedicated. We'll provide our data flow diagram and DPA.
Lena (AE): Billing during POC — they want no surprises. Can we offer a flat POC fee + a clear per-token overage rate?
Rina (Sales Eng): Yes: propose a $2k flat credit covering up to X tokens, then $Y per 1k tokens over. We'll include a daily usage webhook and a cap that halts requests at threshold if they want.
Bright (Customer): Also want deterministic sampling for A/B tests. Is there a way to fix seeds?
Omar (SE): We support deterministic decode by fixing the sampling seed + forcing top_k/top_p. We'll expose that in the shim & eval harness. Note: exact parity still depends on tokenizers.
Rina (Sales Eng): For acceptance criteria, propose: streaming chunk alignment >= 95% identical boundaries (allowing small timing variance), semantic embedding cosine >= 0.9, and <8% token_count difference across prompts. Human review pass 85% on high-priority flows.
Felix (Eng): Timeline: Day 0: IP allowlist & creds, Day 1-2: shim deploy + traffic mirror, Day 3-7: run parity tests, Day 8-10: tune sampling/quantization, Day 11-14: report + handoff.
Lena (AE): Blockers: if they require zero-copy streaming identical chunking at byte-level we may need client changes. Also customer KMS in hosted mode is a blocker.
Bright (Customer): We'll share 150 staging prompts and a sampled traffic replay. Also need SOW & temporary NDA.
Omar (SE): I'll prepare the eval harness link and a sample diff report (CSV: prompt, compx_resp, redwood_resp, chunk_diff_pct, emb_cos).
InfraBot: POC space provisioned: space-bright-poc (id: poc-1933). Invite sent to Lena, Omar, Rina, Jules, Felix.
Jules (Security): I'll attach the minimal security checklist and pen-test timeline.
Lena (AE): Next steps: Rina to send pricing cap, Omar to deploy shim and eval harness, Jules to share security doc, Bright to send prompts + replay by EOD Thursday. :calendar: :white_check_mark:
